newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen firmer at noon, shrug off EPA report.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen firmer at noon, shrug off EPA report.

text.p: The key March three-month Euroyen futures contract was firmer at noon on Friday, ignoring a monthly economic report by Japan's Economic Planning Agency (EPA), traders said.
The EPA said that Japan's economy was firming up and that the EPA's assessment of the Japanese economy was half-a-step more optimistic than last month.

"I thought the EPA was turning optimistic toward the economy, but nobody wanted to sell March (Euroyen)," said a European bank trader. The market remained focused on the Bank of Japan's allegedly bearish view of the economy, he added.
Some BOJ officials appear to be telling the market that the central bank would be unable to raise interest rates in the current fiscal year ending March 31, 1998, traders said.
"The market has recently failed to respond to economic data showing a healthy recovery becuase traders are sensing the BOJ's lingering pessimism over the economy," said a city bank trader.

March Euroyen finished the morning session at 99.05, up from 99.02 on Thursday. A major city bank received fixed interest rates intermittently in the swap market, adding to bullish sentiment, traders said.
